APR (annual percentage rate).definition: The yearly cost of the loan, including interest and certain fees, shown as a percent.

Actual cash value (ACV).definition: What an item is worth today after subtracting for age and wear.

Adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM).definition: A loan whose interest rate can go up or down after a starting period.

Appraisal.definition: A licensed appraiser's written opinion of what the home is worth, ordered for the lender.

Area median income (AMI).definition: The middle household income for an area, used to set income limits such as 65%, 80% or 120% of AMI.

Assessed value.definition: The value the county assessor puts on your property for tax purposes.

Broker (real estate).definition: Washington's license name for the person most people call a real estate agent.

Brokerage services agreement.definition: The written contract between you and a real estate firm that appoints your broker and sets the term, exclusivity and pay.

Certificate of Eligibility (COE).definition: The VA document that shows a lender you qualify for the VA home loan benefit.

Chattel loan.definition: A loan secured only by a manufactured home as personal property, not by land.

Closing.definition: The point when the sale is finished: papers signed, money moved and deed recorded.

Closing Disclosure.definition: The five-page federal form with your final loan terms and costs, which you must get at least three business days before closing.

Closing agent / escrow agent.definition: The neutral, licensed party that holds the money and documents and carries out both sides' written instructions to complete the sale.

Closing costs.definition: The fees and prepaid items you pay to finish the loan and the purchase, separate from the down payment.

Community property.definition: Property acquired during a marriage or registered domestic partnership, which both spouses or partners own together under Washington law.

Condominium.definition: A form of ownership where you own your unit and share ownership of the common elements with the other owners.

Conforming loan.definition: A conventional loan small enough for Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac to buy.

Contingency.definition: A condition in the contract that must be met, or that lets a party end the deal, by a deadline.

Conventional loan.definition: Any home loan that is not insured or guaranteed by a government agency.

Credit score.definition: A number calculated from your credit report that lenders use to judge how risky it is to lend to you.

Debt-to-income ratio (DTI).definition: Your total monthly debt payments divided by your gross monthly income.

Deductible.definition: The part of a covered loss you pay before the insurer pays.

Deed.definition: The document that transfers ownership of the home from the seller to you.

Deed of trust.definition: The recorded document that pledges the home as security for the loan by conveying it to a neutral trustee, who can sell it if the loan is not paid.

Discount point.definition: A fee equal to 1% of the loan amount that you may pay at closing to get a lower interest rate.

Down payment.definition: The part of the purchase price you pay in cash instead of borrowing.

Down payment assistance (DPA).definition: Money, usually a second loan, that helps cover your down payment and closing costs.

Earnest money.definition: A good-faith deposit you make after your offer is accepted, held by a neutral party and applied to your purchase.

Escrow (impound) account.definition: An account your loan servicer uses to collect and pay your property taxes and homeowners insurance.

FHA loan.definition: A loan made by an FHA-approved lender and insured by the Federal Housing Administration.

First-time homebuyer (Commission meaning.definition: A person who has not owned and lived in a primary residence at any time in the past three years.

Fixed-rate mortgage.definition: A loan whose interest rate is set at the start and never changes.

Form 17.definition: The common name for the seller disclosure statement whose content is set by state law.

Funding fee (VA).definition: A one-time charge on most VA loans, set as a percent of the loan amount, that can be added to the loan.

Gift funds.definition: Money given to you, not loaned, by an allowed donor such as a relative for your down payment or closing costs.

HO-6 policy (unit-owner policy).definition: Insurance a condo owner buys for the inside of the unit, belongings and personal liability.

HOA dues (assessments).definition: Regular payments owners make to the association for shared costs, usually separate from the mortgage payment.

Home inspection.definition: A licensed inspector's visual check of a home's current condition, written up in a report for you.

Home inspector.definition: A person licensed by the Washington Department of Licensing to do home inspections.

Home warranty.definition: A service contract that pays for some appliance and system repairs; it is not homeowners insurance.

Homebuyer education class.definition: A free class of about five hours, sponsored by the Housing Finance Commission, that explains the buying process.

Homeowners insurance.definition: Insurance on the house that your lender will require before closing.

Housing counseling.definition: One-on-one advice from a trained counselor on buying, budgeting, credit or avoiding foreclosure.

Inspection contingency.definition: A part of your offer that lets you negotiate or cancel based on what the inspection finds.

Irrigation assessment.definition: The yearly charge an irrigation district puts on a parcel, owed whether or not you use the water.

Jumbo loan.definition: A loan larger than the conforming loan limit.

Lender.definition: The bank, credit union or company that actually loans you the money.

Lender's title policy.definition: Title insurance that protects only the lender, up to the loan amount.

Lien.definition: A legal claim on your property for an unpaid debt.

Limited practice officer (LPO).definition: A non-lawyer licensed by the Washington Supreme Court to select, prepare and complete approved closing documents.

Loan Estimate.definition: The three-page federal form showing a loan's estimated terms and costs, due within three business days of applying.

Loan officer / mortgage loan originator.definition: The licensed or registered person who takes your application and helps you get the loan.

Manufactured home.definition: A factory-built home on a permanent frame, built to the HUD Code on or after June 15, 1976.

Master policy.definition: The association's insurance on shared buildings and common areas, paid from dues.

Mortgage broker.definition: A person or company that does not lend money but helps you find a lender or loan.

Mortgage insurance.definition: Insurance you pay for that protects the lender, not you, if you stop paying.

Mutual acceptance.definition: The moment both buyer and seller have signed and agreed to the same contract terms, from which contract and disclosure deadlines run.

Owner's title policy.definition: Optional title insurance that protects you, the buyer, usually for the full price.

PITI.definition: Principal, interest, taxes and insurance: the four basic parts of a monthly mortgage payment.

PMI (private mortgage insurance).definition: Mortgage insurance on a conventional loan, usually required when the down payment is under 20%.

PUD (planned unit development).definition: A lender's term for a development where you own your lot and home and must belong to an HOA that owns common property.

Payment-deferred loan (silent second).definition: A second loan with no monthly payments that comes due later, such as when you sell, refinance or move out.

Pre-inspection agreement.definition: The written contract you and the inspector sign that says what will and will not be inspected and what it costs.

Preapproval / prequalification.definition: A lender's letter saying about how much it would likely lend you; neither is a guaranteed loan offer.

Preliminary commitment (preliminary titl.definition: The title company's offer to issue a policy subject to listed exceptions; by statute it is not a statement about the condition of title.

Radon.definition: A natural radioactive gas you cannot see or smell that can build up indoors.

Rate lock.definition: A lender's promise to hold your interest rate for a set time, usually 30, 45 or 60 days.

Real estate excise tax (REET).definition: Washington's tax on the sale of real estate, owed by the seller.

Recording.definition: Filing the deed and deed of trust with the county auditor so they become public record.

Renovation loan.definition: One loan that covers both buying the home and paying for repairs.

Replacement cost.definition: What it costs to repair or replace something at today's prices with no subtraction for age.

Resale certificate.definition: A packet from the HOA, provided through the seller, showing dues, special assessments, reserves, insurance, lawsuits and rules for a unit being resold.

Rescind.definition: To cancel the contract and undo the deal, as the buyer may do within three business days of getting the seller disclosure statement.

Reserve study.definition: The association's long-range plan for paying for major repairs and replacements.

Seller disclosure statement.definition: The form required by state law on which the seller answers, from actual knowledge, questions about the property; it is not a warranty.

Servicer.definition: The company that collects your mortgage payment and manages the loan day to day.

Sewer scope.definition: A camera inspection of the sewer pipe.

Special assessment.definition: A one-time or extra HOA charge for a cost not covered by regular dues or reserves.

Statutory warranty deed.definition: A deed in which the seller promises they own the property, that it is free of claims, and that they will defend the buyer's title.

Structural pest inspector (SPI).definition: A person licensed by the Washington State Department of Agriculture to inspect for wood-destroying organisms.

Title elimination.definition: The Washington process that cancels a manufactured home's vehicle-style title and records the home as real property with the land.

Title insurance.definition: A one-time-premium policy that covers losses from hidden problems with ownership, such as old liens or forged documents.

USDA Direct loan.definition: A home loan made by USDA itself to low- and very-low-income buyers in eligible rural areas.

USDA Guaranteed loan.definition: A zero-down home loan made by a USDA-approved lender and backed by USDA, for eligible rural areas and incomes.

Underwriter / underwriting.definition: The lender's review of your income, debts, credit and the property to decide whether to approve the loan.

VA-backed loan.definition: A home loan from a private lender with part of it guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs, for eligible veterans, service members and survivors.

Walk-through.definition: Your last visit to the home before signing, to confirm its condition and any agreed repairs.

Wire recall.definition: A request to your bank to pull back a wire transfer, which works best if made at once.
